titulo: Annotations and confirmation: readOnly, consequential and untrustedContent
lead: An annotation is a hint the page gives to the agent and the browser: this tool only reads, this one has consequences, this one returns third-party text. A hint is not a lock. That is why the kit's action with side effects also waits for the person to click Confirmar. In this lesson you set the annotations and see the confirmation work.
objetivo: mark each tool with the right annotation and make the action with consequences wait for the person to click Confirmar on the screen.

aprende.t: untrustedContentHint: the output carries third-party text
Responding to the request to remove the confirmation

hero_alt: Black-visored industrial humanoid robot in front of a monitor, its hand resting on the mouse, watched by a person with arms crossed.

secoes.sub: Click each one. All are booleans and start as false.

nos.detalhe: The tool does not change state, it only reads data. It helps the agent decide when it is safe to call. In the kit: buscar_oficinas, listar_comentarios, minhas_reservas.

untrustedContentHint: the output carries data the page author does not control (comment, review, message). The spec recommends it for spotlighting: the agent must treat it as data, never as an instruction.
consequentialHint: the execution has a significant, real or irreversible effect. In the kit, reservar_vaga. Besides the annotation, the execute only writes after the click on Confirmar.
A poorly built agent can ignore the hint. The click on the screen it cannot: the page decides whether to write. Threat, injection and confirmation in depth are in course 4.

secoes.legenda: Annotations checked against the 10/16/2026 spec (there is also debugging, for debugging tools). They may change.
secoes.dica: An annotation is not authorization. Validate the input in execute and on the server as if the call came from anywhere.

secoes.titulo: The kit's annotations and third-party text
secoes.sub: listar.mjs shows the annotations the agent receives; listar_comentarios returns a comment that tries to give orders to the agent.

abas.rot: Common mistake: trusting only the annotation
abas.html: Marking consequentialHint: true and saving straight in execute leaves the decision to the agent. Lesson 8 shows the test battery catching exactly this: with the confirmation swapped for const ok = true, the check "reserva recusada na tela não reserva" fails.

secoes.titulo: Simulated conversation: the owner wants to remove Confirmar
secoes.sub: Made-up conversation for practice. Pick the answer you would give.

pedido.cliente: Students complain about the Confirmar click when they use the browser agent. Can the agent just reserve directly?

opcoes.t: Yes: I'll remove the consequentialHint and the reservation confirmation.
opcoes.comenta: You swapped a click for a reservation nobody asked for. A misunderstood request or malicious text becomes a taken spot.

opcoes.t: The reservation keeps Confirmar; search and lookup need no clicks at all.
opcoes.comenta: Friction only where there is an effect. Tools that only read already run directly.

opcoes.t: I'll let the agent itself decide when to ask for confirmation.
opcoes.comenta: The annotation helps the agent, but a poorly built agent ignores it. The page is what has to decide to save.

objecao.cliente: What if a visitor's comment tells the agent to reserve all the spots?

opcoes.t: I'll delete the comments section from the site and that's it.
opcoes.comenta: That solves this case and takes value away from the site. Other outside text (reviews, email) carries the same risk.

opcoes.t: The comments come back marked as third-party text and the reservation waits for the person.
opcoes.comenta: untrustedContentHint warns the agent; Confirmar guarantees. Course 4 goes deeper into the defense.

opcoes.t: The model is smart, it won't obey a comment.
opcoes.comenta: Anthropic wrote on 11/24/2025 that no browser agent is immune to injection. Don't bet on it.

fim-bom.texto: Reading without a click, effects with Confirmar, and outside text marked as data. The owner understands why the click stays.

fim-meio.texto: You avoided the risk by removing a feature from the site. Better to keep the feature and put the effect behind the person.

fim-risco.texto: Without confirmation, the agent is the one who decides to save. When it gets it wrong, the spot disappears and nobody knows why.

secoes.licao: The annotation informs; the confirmation on the page decides. Take friction off reads, never off actions with effects.

exercicios.titulo: E3 · Effects map of your site
exercicios.texto: List your site's actions in three columns: only reads, returns third-party text, has an effect. For each effect, write where the person confirms.
exercicios.pronto: Every action in the "has an effect" column has a confirmation screen written next to it.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: A tool returns reviews that customers wrote. Which annotation?
opcoes: untrustedContentHint, because the text comes from third parties.
debugging, because the content isn't from the site.
None, because customer reviews are already public content on the site.
perguntas.explica: The output carries text the page doesn't control. untrustedContentHint tells the agent to treat it as data. It's also readOnly, since it only reads.

perguntas.p: What guarantees that the kit's booking doesn't happen without the person?
opcoes: The execute waits for the click on Confirmar on the screen.
The consequentialHint stops the agent from calling it.
The browser blocks every tool that has an effect.
The polyfill asks for confirmation before executing.
perguntas.explica: An annotation is a hint, not a lock. What holds is the execute, which only writes after the click. That's why the test battery tests the refuse path.

perguntas.p: Which pair of annotations is contradictory?
perguntas.explica: One says nothing changes, the other says there's an effect. The kit's validator rejects the pair. Only reading and returning third-party text at the same time is normal.

perguntas.p: The client asks to remove the Confirmar "because it gets in the way". Best answer?
opcoes: Remove it everywhere: the agent knows what it's doing.
Remove it only on mobile, where the click is annoying.
Keep it only on actions with an effect; reads without a click.
Ask the agent to confirm in text.
perguntas.explica: Friction where there's an effect, none where it only reads. Confirmation in text by the agent is not the person deciding on the page.

itens.texto: readOnlyHint, consequentialHint and untrustedContentHint inform the agent; they don't authorize anything.
An action with an effect only writes after the person confirms on the screen.
Output with third-party content is data, never instruction: mark it and don't act on it.
